govdocs-archive_org-mkultra-the-hidden-r:
MKULTRA was the CIA's secret program of experiments in mind control, run for two decades and exposed in the 1970s. MKULTRA: The Hidden Record presents the complete official congressional hearing on the program, from the House Task Force on the Declassification of Federal Secrets, in a large-print edition.

The hearing takes up mind control and accountability together: what the agency did to its subjects, what records survived, and who answered for it. Witnesses and documents are given in full rather than summarized. For researchers, a complete hearing transcript is the raw material from which every later account of MKULTRA is built.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-Pre-Assassinati:
An unidentified author left this memoir excerpt about two dogs, Lady and Chicha. The writer describes farm life with them. Lady hunted rabbits. One morning, Lady chased off a Dalmatian and a German shepherd that had each seized a pullet, a young hen, from the yard.

Personal writing like this sits oddly in assassination files, and that is part of its record. Researchers' papers held their whole lives, not only their cases. The excerpt is plain farm writing: animals named, habits noted, one morning's alarm told in order. It preserves the voice of a man better known, in these files, for geese, letters, and inquiries, remembering two dogs on a farm.

A letter dated November 9, 1942 accepts a job offer from Julian P. Brodie of Green-Brodie, Inc. The pay was 25 dollars a week. Wartime Washington ran on such letters: a firm offers, a man accepts, terms in a paragraph. The author's name cannot be recovered from the text. The file preserves the acceptance and the wage, a small fixed point in one working life during the war's first year.
govdocs-archive_org-the-crystal-book-of-: Gustavo Brondino's Treatise on the Hyperborean Gnosis appears here as the title page of The Crystal Book of Agartha, volume 2. Agartha is a legendary hidden kingdom in esoteric writing. The library holds the item as an archive piece, without taking a stance, and classes the material as esoteric. A title page is a threshold only: it names a hidden treatise that promises secret teaching about a hidden world.
